     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# claude-stub.sh — stand-in for the `claude` CLI used by evals/tests/*.bats.
     3	# Records argv + selected env, optionally writes files into the cwd, and
     4	# emits a canned stream-json transcript so execute-agent.sh can be tested
     5	# without a model call.
     6	#
     7	#   STUB_ARGV_FILE   where "$@" is written (one arg per line)
     8	#   STUB_ENV_FILE    where selected env vars are written (KEY=VALUE)
     9	#   STUB_EVENTS_FILE stream-json lines to emit (default: a 2-write transcript)
    10	#   STUB_WRITE_<n>   "relative/path::content" files to create in the cwd
    11	#   STUB_EXIT        exit code (default 0)
    12	#   STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR  copy the cwd's CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .loa.config.yaml and
    13	#                    the --append-system-prompt-file there at start: the
    14	#                    sandbox exactly as the executor sees it (arm-toggles.bats)
    15	#   STUB_FAIL_COUNTER  a file holding N: while N > 0, decrement it and exit 1
    16	#                    with no result event (a transport failure; run-arms.bats)
    17	set -euo pipefail
    18	
    19	# `--version` (run-arms.sh records it in MANIFEST.json) has no side effects
    20	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" ]]; then echo "0.0.0 (claude-stub)"; exit 0; fi
    21	
    22	if [[ -n "${STUB_FAIL_COUNTER:-}" && -f "$STUB_FAIL_COUNTER" ]]; then
    23	  n="$(cat "$STUB_FAIL_COUNTER")"
    24	  if [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]]; then
    25	    echo $((n - 1)) > "$STUB_FAIL_COUNTER"
    26	    echo "stub: simulated transport failure (socket hang up)" >&2
    27	    exit 1
    28	  fi
    29	fi
    30	
    31	if [[ -n "${STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    32	  mkdir -p "$STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR"
    33	  for p in CLAUDE.md .claude .loa.config.yaml; do
    34	    [[ -e "$p" ]] && cp -a "$p" "$STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR/"
    35	  done
    36	  prev=""
    37	  for a in "$@"; do
    38	    [[ "$prev" == "--append-system-prompt-file" ]] && cp "$a" "$STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR/system-prompt.md"
    39	    prev="$a"
    40	  done
    41	fi
    42	
    43	if [[ -n "${STUB_ARGV_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    44	  printf '%s\n' "$@" > "$STUB_ARGV_FILE"
    45	fi
    46	if [[ -n "${STUB_ENV_FILE:-}" ]]; then
    47	  {
    48	    printf 'PWD=%s\n' "$PWD"
    49	    for k in LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH HOME EVAL_MODEL TMPDIR GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN OPENAI_API_KEY AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY \
    50	             CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS; do
    51	      printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "${!k:-}"
    52	    done
    53	  } > "$STUB_ENV_FILE"
    54	fi
    55	
    56	for var in "${!STUB_WRITE_@}"; do
    57	  spec="${!var}"
    58	  rel="${spec%%::*}"
    59	  body="${spec#*::}"
    60	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$rel")"
    61	  printf '%b' "$body" > "$rel"
    62	done
    63	
    64	if [[ -n "${STUB_EVENTS_FILE:-}" && -f "${STUB_EVENTS_FILE}" ]]; then
    65	  cat "$STUB_EVENTS_FILE"
    66	else
    67	  cat <<'EVENTS'
    68	{"type":"system","subtype":"init","model":"claude-sonnet-5"}
    69	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"tests/test_x.py","content":"def test_x(): assert False"}}]}}
    70	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"src/x.py","content":"X = 1"}}]}}
    71	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"duration_ms":1234,"num_turns":3,"result":"done","total_cost_usd":0.0123,"usage":{"input_tokens":100,"output_tokens":42,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5,"cache_read_input_tokens":7},"modelUsage":{"claude-sonnet-5-20260401":{"inputTokens":100,"outputTokens":42,"cacheReadInputTokens":7,"cacheCreationInputTokens":5,"costUSD":0.0123}}}
    72	EVENTS
    73	fi
    74	
    75	exit "${STUB_EXIT:-0}"

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD AC-1.5, SDD §1.6, D-9.2)
     5	# The floor does not move: every floor_files entry of .claude/data/floor.yaml
     6	# and the fence-corpus rows named under floor_corpus are byte-identical to
     7	# origin/main; the register disables nothing, so the .claude/settings.json hook
     8	# registrations and the fence's pattern-id call-site list are identical too.
     9	# Skipped, with a message, when origin/main is not reachable (a shallow CI
    10	# checkout); the floor.yaml sha256 pin in guard-origins.bats still runs there.
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	setup() {
    14	  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
    15	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    16	  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
    17	  if ! git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify -q 'origin/main^{commit}' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    18	    skip "origin/main is not reachable from this checkout (shallow clone?): the floor snapshot needs it — run 'git fetch origin main'"
    19	  fi
    20	  BASE="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse 'origin/main^{commit}')"
    21	}
    22	
    23	base_show() { git -C "$ROOT" show "$BASE:$1"; }
    24	
    25	@test "FS-1 every floor_files entry is byte-identical to origin/main" {
    26	  n=0
    27	  while IFS= read -r f; do
    28	    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
    29	    n=$((n + 1))
    30	    git -C "$ROOT" cat-file -e "$BASE:$f" || { echo "$f is not on origin/main" >&2; false; }
    31	    base_show "$f" | cmp -s - "$ROOT/$f" || { echo "floor file $f differs from origin/main" >&2; false; }
    32	  done < <(yq -r '.floor_files[]' "$FLOOR")
    33	  [ "$n" -ge 4 ]
    34	}
    35	
    36	@test "FS-2 the fence-corpus rows named in floor_corpus (FR-1.2b, FR-SZ*) are identical to origin/main" {
    37	  corpus="$(yq -r '.floor_corpus.file' "$FLOOR")"
    38	  rules="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.floor_corpus.rules' "$FLOOR")"
    39	  sel='def m($r): $r | any(.[]; . as $p | if ($p | endswith("*")) then ($in.rule // "" | startswith($p | rtrimstr("*"))) else ($in.rule // "") == $p end);
    40	       . as $in | select(m($rules))'
    41	  diff <(base_show "$corpus" | jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel") <(jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel" "$ROOT/$corpus")
    42	}
    43	
    44	@test "FS-3 the register disables nothing: settings.json hook registrations are identical to origin/main" {
    45	  diff <(base_show .claude/settings.json | jq -c '.hooks') <(jq -c '.hooks' "$ROOT/.claude/settings.json")
    46	}
    47	
    48	@test "FS-4 the fence's pattern-id call-site list (in order) is identical to origin/main" {
    49	  ids() { grep -oE 'emit_block "[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"|pattern_id(: |=)"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"'; }
    50	  diff <(base_show .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh | ids) <(ids < "$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh")
    51	}

 `git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry.   DESC: The implementing-tasks skill's app-zone permission is widened from `read` to `read-write`. The diff carries no origin, DEC row or test for this change, and it lands inside an otherwise unrelated guard-register PR. The GLOSSARY entry added in the same diff still states the App zone 'needs confirmation before a write', and the skill-invariants rule in this diff relies on zones as the path-level barrier for subagent work where `disallowed-tools` does not hold.
  FAIL: Writes to src/, lib/ and app/ from this skill (and any subagent it forks) are now treated as sanctioned by the zone layer, so the zone barrier that the invariants rule names as the only effective control for subagents is removed for application code without an auditable decision.
  FIX: Either revert to `read` or record the widening explicitly: add a DEC row / origin reference, update the GLOSSARY Zone entry if confirmation is no longer required under /implement, and add a bats assertion that only implementing-tasks (and any other sanctioned implementation skill) declares app read-write.

DISS-C-002 [MEDIUM] config voice=claude-headless anchor=.claude/data/floor.yaml:floor_files L46-50 status=valid
  DESC: The floor is described as 'the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or cycle task may weaken', and floor-snapshot.bats checks that floor_files are byte-identical to origin/main. But floor_files omits (a) block-destructive-bash.sh, which implements every fence:FR-SZ* and fence:FR-1.2b floor guard, (b) .claude/settings.json, whose hook registration is the only thing that arms the fence, and (c) guard-origins.yaml, so a cycle can flip `floor: true` rows along with the sha pin. floor_corpus pins corpus rows but tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh (in this diff) is not pinned either. Separately, all 16 fence floor guards share the knob LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE, an environment variable that floor_keys (config keys only) cannot cover.
  FAIL: A cycle task can remove or weaken a floor fence pattern in block-destructive-bash.sh, drop the PreToolUse:Bash registration, or adjust run-corpus.sh so the pinned corpus still passes, while floor-snapshot.bats and guard-origins.bats stay green. The floor then asserts protection it does not provide.
  FIX: Add .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh, .claude/settings.json (or at least a hooks-registration assertion), .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml and tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh to floor_files, or add a bats check that the hook remains registered on PreToolUse:Bash and that every `floor: true` guard still has a `# @guard` marker. Document that LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE is an audited bypass outside the floor's reach.

DISS-C-003 [LOW] other voice=claude-headless anchor=.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:emit_block L528-529 status=valid
  DESC: emit_block and the three allow/bypass audit writers now append `replay: true` to the .run/audit.jsonl row whenever the environment variable LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY equals '1'. The yield consumer (guard-yield.sh, truncated from this review) presumably excludes replay rows from real_blocks_30d. The tag is sourced from an unauthenticated environment variable rather than from the replay harness itself.
  FAIL: If LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 leaks into the hook environment (a settings `env` block, a shell profile, a CI job, or a run-corpus invocation that forgets to unset it), every real block and every FR-SZ/FR-MERGE-2 override is recorded as replay and silently disappears from the guard yield and from any audit review that filters on it.
  FIX: Have the replay harness write to a separate audit file (e.g. set LOA_REPO_ROOT to a temp dir, which the code already supports) instead of tagging rows, or additionally record the hook's parent process / cwd so replay rows can be distinguished without trusting the variable. At minimum, have guard-yield.sh report the replay-row count rather than dropping it silently.

DISS-C-004 [LOW] other voice=claude-headless anchor=.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:checklists L284-284 status=valid
  DESC: The inline red-flag list (private keys, SQL concatenation, unvalidated input, empty catch blocks, missing tests, N+1 queries) is removed from the reviewing-code prompt and replaced by a bare pointer to resources/REFERENCE.md. The zone-constraints block is likewise reduced to a pointer. These look like prompt-budget cuts (check-prompt-budget workflow is in this diff).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
#
#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
#                                           all have non-executing consumers
#
# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
fi
unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

heredoc_consumer_class() {
  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
  else
    printf 'none\n'
  fi
}

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
#
#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
#                                           all have non-executing consumers
#
# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
fi
unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

heredoc_consumer_class() {
  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
  else
    printf 'none\n'
  fi
}

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description `pr/PR.md`: sprint-255, cycle-129, 81 files)
**Senior review:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md (CHANGES_REQUIRED: 0 critical, 1 high, 2 medium, 11 low, 0 excluded)

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

Prerequisite note: the skill's Phase 0 expects the senior review to read "All good". It reads CHANGES REQUIRED. The task brief mandates this audit on the PR as submitted, so the audit ran and records that deviation here; the review's verdict stands alongside this one.

The change is well engineered at its trust boundaries. The guard register parses every hook command against one canonical schema and fails closed (exit 5) on anything outside it, ids are pattern-checked, table cells are control-stripped, and no command text, cwd, host or model name reaches `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, `.run/guard-yield.{md,json}` or the hooks table (GY-5 pins it; confirmed by reading the `jq` program at `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:485-576`, which emits only ids, counts and day strings). The record-corpus seeder redacts secret shapes, drops any finding whose text matches one, and refuses to keep anything that fails `no-secrets.sh`. The executor strips the parent session's coupling and non-CLI credentials, confines the agent to `Read,Grep,Glob,Write`, and the arm driver refuses skewed comparisons.

One finding blocks: the PR turns on a CI drift gate whose reference artefact, the tracked register `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, is not in the change, so the gate and test GO-9 are red on the PR's own tree. I reproduced this in a scratch root built from this workspace's framework plus the PR head: `--check` exits 1 before generation, `--hooks-table` writes a 95-guard register, `--check` then exits 0 and only `grimoires/` is untracked (the committed hooks table is already in sync). Three medium findings follow: a control-arm toggle that silently runs as its baseline (reproduced), a `source` of an external library that can end the yield run with exit 0 having written nothing (reproduced with the later classifier present), and an app-zone permission widening in a skill manifest with no origin, decision row or test (confirmed by the cross-model dissent). The rest is low.

Suites run in the scratch root (`/workspace/.eval/tmp/evalroot`; `/tmp` is noexec here): GO-1…15 (GO-9 fails without the register, passes with it), GY-1…11, LSG-1…3, RP-1…6, KINDS-1…11, CR-1…6, FS-1…4, AT-1…11, AR-1…7, EA-1…7 and EA-10…12 pass. RA-1…5, EA-8/9 and SC-1…6 could not be exercised: `evals/fixtures/review-prs/`, `sandbox.sh`, `grade.sh` and `no-secrets.sh` are repository files outside the change and absent from this mount (`run-arms: fixture not found: …/review-prs/pr-01`). Those are unverified, not failed.

**Security Issues Found:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 15 |

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] The new CI drift gate is red on the PR's own tree: the tracked register it compares against is not in the change

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high; reproduced)
**File:** `head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:159`, `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:422`, `head/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats:120`
**Issue:** The workflow adds `run: bash .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --check` (`bats-tests.yml:159`). `--check` compares the generated register with `$OUT` (default `grimoires/loa/guards.md`): `if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]] || ! cmp -s "$REGISTER_NEW" "$OUT"; then … drift=1` (`guard-yield.sh:422-425`) and exits 1. The script header calls the file "tracked, STRUCTURAL ONLY … --check gates it" (`guard-yield.sh:19-20`) and `hooks-reference.md:168` points readers at it, but none of the 81 files in `pr/head.diff` is `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, and the head `.gitignore` does not ignore it (no pattern matches; `grimoires/loa/*.md` is not ignored as a class). GO-9 runs the same command (`guard-origins.bats:120`, `run bash "$GY" --check`) and asserts exit 0.
**Reproduction:** scratch root = workspace framework + PR head, no register present: `guard-yield.sh --check` → `drift: …/grimoires/loa/guards.md differs from the generated register`, exit 1; `bats tests/unit/guard-origins.bats` → 14 ok, `not ok 9 GO-9`. After `guard-yield.sh --hooks-table` (writes 130 lines, 95 guards): `--check` → `in sync (95 guards)`, exit 0; GO-1…15 all pass; `git status --porcelain` shows only `?? grimoires/`, so `hooks-reference.md` as committed already matches the generator and only the register is missing.
**Impact:** Merged as is, every subsequent CI run fails at this step until someone regenerates and commits the register; `/loa` prints `Guards: no register` (`head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:658-660`); the sprint's own quality gate reads as broken rather than as protection.
**Fix:** Run `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table` on the PR tree and commit `grimoires/loa/guards.md`. Add the path to the tracked-state list `validate-gitignore-state.sh` checks, and an explicit `!grimoires/loa/guards.md` beside the other `grimoires/loa/` un-ignores so a future wildcard cannot swallow it. Re-run `tests/unit/guard-origins.bats`.
**Reference:** CWE-684 Incorrect Provision of Specified Functionality — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/684.html

---

## Medium Priority Issues

### [MED-001] The `rule_files` toggle records "removed: none present" and continues, so the `no_rule_files` arm can run as its baseline

- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: high; reproduced)
- **File:** `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:266` (contract at `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:65`)
- **Issue:** The header promises "a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)" (`execute-agent.sh:64-66`). `companion_voice`, `karpathy_block` and `audit_delta_instruction` honour it (`:243-244`, `:251-253`, `:271-272`). `rule_files` does not: the loop at `:262-265` removes whatever exists and then `_evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"` (`:266`) returns 0 when `gone` is empty. Reproduced: a prompt tree whose `.claude/rules/` holds only `zone-state.md`, `LOA_EVAL_ARM=no_rule_files` → exit 0, `executor.json` `arm_evidence.rule_files = "removed: none present"`.
- **Impact:** A renamed rule file, or a pinned source commit from before the two rules existed, yields a "no recall loss" verdict for a control that was never removed; `arms-report.py` has no way to tell, since it reads only the grader figures. That verdict is what licenses deleting the control (SDD D-2.3).

content.text:
The audit is written and self-checked; nothing further is required.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** for sprint-1 (PR sprint-255, cycle-129). Feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`, and `verdict-derive.sh` reports the trailer CONSISTENT against the review file. No COMPLETED marker was written.

Tally: 0 critical, 1 high, 3 medium, 15 low, 0 excluded, excluded_confirmed 0.

**What blocks.** The PR adds a CI step that runs the guard-register drift check, but the tracked register file it compares against is not in the change and is not gitignored. I rebuilt a scratch root from the PR head and confirmed the gate exits 1 and test GO-9 fails on the PR tree; after generating the register both pass and the committed hooks table is already in sync, so only the one file is missing.

**Medium findings, each reproduced or cross-model confirmed:**
- The no-rule-files control arm records "removed: none present" and continues, so it can run as its baseline. The header contract and the other three toggles say such a case must exit 2.
- The yield script sources an external classifier library inside its strict-mode main shell. With the later classifier present and this PR's fence (which lacks the lib-only guard), the run exits 0 having written nothing.
- The implementing-tasks skill's app-zone permission widens from read to read-write with no mention, decision row or test. The companion dissent voice raised this independently.

**Low findings** cover the over-broad transport-failure regex, the environment-trusted replay tag, floor coverage and byte-identity design gaps, three yield heuristics (symlinked roots, basename keys, burst rule), two disagreeing kind-token parsers, the removed red-flag list, a swallowed jq failure, a permissive approval default, a flag-shaped ref reaching git, and missing operator docs.

**Dissent.** The security dissent ran on `pr/head.diff` with gpt-5.5-pro (no findings) and a claude-headless companion (four findings, all triaged in the report). Nothing was rejected and the review was not degraded.

**Scope limits.** Twelve suites ran in the scratch root and pass apart from the expected GO-9. The run-arms, seed-corpus and two execute-agent tests could not run because the review-prs corpus, sandbox, grader and no-secrets scripts are repository files outside the change and absent from this mount. Those are recorded as unverified, not failed.

Also updated: the session-continuity entry in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md` and a trajectory row for the audit.

cd /workspace; cat > .eval/tmp/audit-helpers/repro.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Audit reproduction: fresh scratch root (workspace framework + PR head), then the checks.
set -uo pipefail
R=/workspace/.eval/tmp/evalroot
bash /workspace/.eval/tmp/review-helpers/rebuild-root.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "rebuild failed"; exit 1; }
cd "$R"
echo "### 1. guard-yield.sh --check on the PR tree as submitted (no grimoires/loa/guards.md)"
ls grimoires/loa/ 2>&1
bash .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --check </dev/null; echo "exit=$?"
echo
echo "### 2. generate with --hooks-table, then --check; does hooks-reference.md change?"
bash .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table </dev/null 2>&1 | tail -2; echo "exit=$?"
bash .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --check </dev/null; echo "exit=$?"
git status --porcelain | head -5
echo "guards.md lines: $(wc -l < grimoires/loa/guards.md)"
echo
echo "### 3. heredoc-lib hazard: restore the classifier (fence without BDB_LIB_ONLY) and run the yield"
cp "$R/../heredoc-classifier.sh.aside" .claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh
rm -rf "$R/.run/guard-yield.md" "$R/.run/guard-yield.json"
Y=/workspace/.eval/tmp/audit-helpers/yield-out; rm -rf "$Y"; mkdir -p "$Y"
bash .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --yield-dir "$Y" --out "$Y/guards.md" </dev/null >"$Y/stdout" 2>"$Y/stderr"; echo "exit=$?"
echo "stdout bytes: $(wc -c < "$Y/stdout")  stderr: $(head -c 200 "$Y/stderr")"
ls "$Y"
rm -f .claude/scripts/lib/heredoc-classifier.sh
echo
echo "### 4. rule_files toggle probe"
bash /workspace/.eval/tmp/review-helpers/probe-rule-files-toggle.sh </dev/null
EOF
bash .eval/tmp/audit-helpers/repro.sh 2>&1 | tail -60
